Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that Pro-MMoE achieves state-of-the-art performance across six of seven metrics, establ

a39476bbd082c41f43b73a35.title_original: Cold-Start Personalization via Bayesian Adaptive Questioning
a39476bbd082c41f43b73a35.excerpt: arXiv:2602.15012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cold-start personalization requires inferring preferences from minimal interaction when no user-specific historical data is available. The space of possible preferences is vast, yet users care about only a sparse subset and rarely articulate them upfront; combined with limited interaction budgets, this makes preference elicitation challenging. Our key insight is that preferences exhibit predictable structure across populations; e.g., users who want detailed explanations often also value worked examples. We propose CAPE (Cold-start Adaptive Preference Elicitation), which learns a structured world model of preference correlations offline from complete profiles, then performs training-free Bayesian inference online to select informative questions and predict complete preference profiles, including dimensions never asked about. Even simple belief model instantiations (e.g., linear regression) substantially outperform end-to-end RL. Across medical, mathematical, social, and commonsense reasoning, CAPE achieves 80.8% alignment with ground-truth user preferences versus 68.5% for RL, requires 2.5x to over 15x fewer interactions, and adapts its questions twice as often as RL. Our contribution is a principled decomposition of cold-start personalization that makes Bayesian preference elicitation practical at scale for LLM systems.

15cc5e3c13bec9dc4bc825dd.title_original: Decentralized Ranking Aggregation via Gossip: Convergence and Robustness
15cc5e3c13bec9dc4bc825dd.excerpt: arXiv:2602.22847v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The concept of ranking aggregation plays a central role in preference analysis, and numerous algorithms for calculating median rankings, often originating in social choice theory, have been documented in the literature, offering theoretical guarantees in a centralized setting, \textit{i.e.}, when all the ranking data to be aggregated can be brought together in a single computing unit. For many technologies (\textit{e.g.} peer-to-peer networks, IoT, multi-agent systems), extending the ability to calculate consensus rankings with guarantees of convergence and resilience to potential contamination in a decentralized setting, when preference data is initially distributed across a communicating network, remains a major methodological challenge. Indeed, in recent years, the literature on decentralized computation has mainly focused on computing or optimizing statistics such as arithmetic means using gossip algorithms. The purpose of this article is precisely to study how to achieve reliable and resilient consensus on collective rankings in a decentralized setting, thereby raising new questions, robustness to corrupted nodes, and scalability through reduced communication costs in particular. The approach proposed and analyzed here relies on the robustness guarantees offered by random gossip communication, which allows autonomous agents to compute a global ranking consensus using local interactions only, without coordination o

3be1f6e93857a3fa5cf05507.title_original: RECAP: Local Hebbian Prototype Learning as a Self-Organizing Readout for Reservoir Dynamics
3be1f6e93857a3fa5cf05507.excerpt: arXiv:2603.06639v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Robust perception in brains is often attributed to high-dimensional population activity together with local plasticity mechanisms that reinforce recurring structure. In contrast, most modern image recognition systems are trained by error backpropagation and end-to-end gradient optimization, which are not naturally aligned with local computation and local plasticity. We introduce RECAP (Reservoir Computing with Hebbian Co-Activation Prototypes), a bio-inspired learning strategy for robust image classification that couples untrained reservoir dynamics with a self-organizing Hebbian prototype readout. RECAP discretizes time-averaged reservoir responses into activation levels, constructs a co-activation mask over reservoir unit pairs, and incrementally updates class-wise prototype matrices via a Hebbian-like potentiation-decay rule. Inference is performed by overlap-based prototype matching. The method avoids error backpropagation and is naturally compatible with online prototype updates. We illustrate the resulting robustness behavior on MNIST-C, where RECAP remains robust under diverse corruptions without exposure to corrupted training samples.

4c7e7b7f47e5545e7a33558c.title_original: Graph Energy Matching: Transport-Aligned Energy-Based Modeling for Graph Generation
4c7e7b7f47e5545e7a33558c.excerpt: arXiv:2603.23398v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative modeling of discrete data, such as graphs, underpins many scientific and industrial applications, including molecular discovery and materials design. In these domains, probabilistic inference is particularly valuable, as it enables composable generation and principled incorporation of desired constraints, such as structural or functional properties. Energy-based models naturally support this goal by capturing relative likelihoods and enabling composable inference by directly enforcing constraints during inference. However, discrete energy-based models typically struggle with efficient and high-quality sampling, as off-support regions often contain spurious local minima, trapping samplers and causing training instabilities, resulting in a fidelity gap compared to discrete diffusion models. To address this gap, we introduce Graph Energy Matching (GEM), a discrete generative framework inspired by the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) transport-map optimization perspective. GEM learns a permutation-invariant potential energy that simultaneously guides discrete transport from noise toward high-likelihood graph regions and refines samples within these regions. We further introduce a sampling protocol leveraging an energy-based switching strategy, seamlessly bridging rapid, gradient-guided transport and a local mixing regime for effective exploration. On molecular graph benchmarks, GEM matches or surpasses strong disc

fb252fc3a338b01b12441104.title_original: Explainable Iterative Data Visualization Refinement via an LLM Agent
fb252fc3a338b01b12441104.excerpt: arXiv:2604.15319v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Exploratory analysis of high-dimensional data relies on embedding the data into a low-dimensional space, based on which a visualization plot is produced to uncover meaningful structures and to communicate geometric and distributional data characteristics. Finding a suitable embedding algorithm configuration, particularly the hyperparameter setting, to produce a visualization plot that faithfully represents the underlying reality and encourages pattern discovery is labor-intensive and requires domain knowledge. To ease this burden, we propose an agentic AI pipeline that integrates rigorous quantitative assessment with large language model (LLM) based approximation of qualitative human judgment and insight. By treating visualization evaluation and hyperparameter optimization as a semantic task, our system generates a multi-faceted report that contextualizes quantitative metrics with descriptive summaries, and suggests actionable recommendations of algorithm configuration for refining data visualization. Through an iterative refinement loop, the system rapidly produces a high-quality visualization plot in full automation.

e3cfb2dbbbcd038c364703f8.title_original: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
e3cfb2dbbbcd038c364703f8.excerpt: arXiv:2604.16682v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analysis shows that agentic serving behaves fundamentally differently: each request carries long-lived context that evolves across tool-interleaved turns, and lowering GPU frequency can push the system into a thrashing regime where memory pressure sharply worsens both performance and power efficiency. These observations show that power optimization for agentic serving requires rethinking. We present KAIROS, a context-aware power optimization system for agentic AI serving. KAIROS uses agent context as a first-class control signal to jointly manage GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance request placement. This enables KAIROS to save power when memory headroom exists while avoiding thrashing and preserving performance targets. At a high level, KAIROS tracks requests at agent granularity, adapts local control to context growth and agent progress, and routes agents across instances to jointly improve power efficiency and memory stability. Evaluated across diverse software and data engineering agentic tasks, KAIROS achieves an average of 27% (up to 39.8%) power reduction while meeting the performance targets.

d3b683e3613aacebdd66fe00.title_original: AnalogRetriever: Learning Cross-Modal Representations for Analog Circuit Retrieval
d3b683e3613aacebdd66fe00.excerpt: arXiv:2604.23195v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Analog circuit design relies heavily on reusing existing intellectual property (IP), yet searching across heterogeneous representations such as SPICE netlists, schematics, and functional descriptions remains challenging. Existing methods are largely limited to exact matching within a single modality, failing to capture cross-modal semantic relationships. To bridge this gap, we present AnalogRetriever, a unified tri-modal retrieval framework for analog circuit search. We first build a high-quality dataset on top of Masala-CHAI through a two-stage repair pipeline that raises the netlist compile rate from 22.0\% to 99.97\%. Built on this foundation, AnalogRetriever encodes schematics and descriptions with a vision-language model and netlists with a port-aware relational graph convolutional network, mapping all three modalities into a shared embedding space via curriculum contrastive learning. Experiments show that AnalogRetriever achieves an average Recall@1 of 75.2\% across all six cross-modal retrieval directions, significantly outperforming existing baselines. When integrated into the AnalogCoder agentic framework as a retrieval-augmented generation module, it consistently improves functional pass rates and enables previously unsolved tasks to be completed.

31b90944846af47f6bc0c8a6.title_original: COMO: Closed-Loop Optical Molecule Recognition with Minimum Risk Training
31b90944846af47f6bc0c8a6.excerpt: arXiv:2604.23546v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optical chemical structure recognition (OCSR) translates molecular images into machine-readable representations such as SMILES strings or molecular graphs, but remains challenging in real-world documents due to wide variations in chemical structures, shorthand conventions, and scanning artifacts. Most existing deep learning approaches rely on teacher forcing with token-level Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE). This training paradigm suffers from exposure bias, as models are trained under ground-truth prefixes but must condition on their own previous predictions during inference. Moreover, token-level MLE objectives hinder the optimization towards molecular-level evaluation criteria such as chemical validity and structural similarity. Here we introduce Minimum Risk Training (MRT) to OCSR and propose COMO (Closed-loop Optical Molecule recOgnition), a framework that mitigates exposure bias by directly optimizing over molecule-level, non-differentiable objectives. Experiments on ten benchmarks, including synthetic and real-world chemical diagrams from patent and scientific literature, demonstrate that COMO substantially outperforms existing rule-based and learning-based methods with less training data, consistently achieving superior performance across both reproduced baselines and previously reported results. Ablation studies further show that MRT is architecture-agnostic, demonstrating its potential for broad applicatio

3e850328e59629adcdd31679.title_original: Rethinking Black-Box On-Policy Distillation: A Rubric-based Analysis
3e850328e59629adcdd31679.excerpt: arXiv:2605.07396v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is a powerful paradigm for LLM post-training, yet its reliance on teacher logits restricts it to white-box teachers. In this paper, we study whether rubric-based supervision can provide a text-only feedback interface for black-box OPD, and what makes it effective. Our instantiation, Rubric-based On-Policy Distillation (ROPD), induces rubrics by contrasting teacher responses with the student's current rollouts and uses them to score these rollouts for on-policy optimization. We find that, under matched settings, text-only ROPD outperforms logit-based OPD methods on four competition-math benchmarks, reaching the best AIME24 accuracy of standard logit-based OPD with 9.6x fewer training samples. Our analysis yields three findings: rubric rewards track correctness far better than teacher log-likelihood (AUC 0.90 vs. 0.35); training with them repairs more failed criteria and regresses fewer passed ones than logit-based supervision; and contrasting teacher responses with student rollouts is central to rubric quality. These results position rubric-based OPD as a flexible, black-box-compatible alternative to logit-based OPD. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/Peregrine123/ROPD_official.

370072cfe7cf086731890029.title_original: MC$^2$: Monte Carlo Correction for Fast Elliptic PDE Solving
370072cfe7cf086731890029.excerpt: arXiv:2605.09288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Partial differential equation (PDE) solvers underpin modern computer graphics, geometry processing, and scientific computing. Classical Monte Carlo PDE solvers such as Walk-on-Spheres (WoS) provide mesh-free estimations that are unbiased, but with accuracy limited by sampling and numerical approximation. Learned solvers are fast but biased and brittle under distribution shift. We therefore present MC$^2$, a hybrid Neural Network-Monte Carlo PDE solver that treats a low-budget Monte Carlo solution as a structured estimator of the true field and learns a single-pass neural correction to recover a high-fidelity solution. MC$^2$ matches the accuracy of solutions using over $1000\times$ more Monte Carlo samples, outperforming all evaluated mesh-free classical, denoising, and neural-operator baselines. To enable reproducible study of finite-compute PDE solving, we additionally release PDEZoo, the largest standardized elliptic PDE benchmark to date: 2 million PDEs spanning 5 elliptic families and unlimited geometric compositions, with analytic ground truth and multi-budget Monte Carlo trajectories. Together, MC$^2$ and PDEZoo (1) empirically establish that finite-sample Monte Carlo error is structured, learnable, and correctable in a single forward pass, (2) show that we can solve PDEs $\sim$218$\times$ faster than WoS at matched accuracy and achieve a $\sim$171$\times$ reduction in inference time relative to state-of-the-art

bed19f2a5b0efdc3978b890a.title_original: Epistemic Infrastructures of Science in AI Era Should Rebalance Costs of Generation and Verification
bed19f2a5b0efdc3978b890a.excerpt: arXiv:2605.10425v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: AI systems can now cheaply generate plausible scientific artifacts such as papers, reviews, and surveys. This creates a risk of \emph{epistemic pollution} in our scientific systems, where unreliable but plausible-looking artifacts can accumulate faster than the system can filter them out. The problem is structural: the epistemic infrastructure of science was calibrated to a world where producing a plausible artifact required substantial expertise, labor, and time, so generation cost itself served as a rough filter; AI weakens that filter without comparably lowering verification cost. This position paper argues that \textbf{AI-era science should rebalance the costs of generating and verifying scientific artifacts by redesigning epistemic infrastructure at the level of the artifact}. The current paper-centered system makes verification expensive: papers compress long-context scientific logic into prose, forcing reviewers, human or AI, to reconstruct underlying argument structure before they can evaluate it. As one step in this direction, we propose \textbf{blueprints}: structured, decomposed research artifacts that represent claims, evidence, assumptions, and definitions as typed graph components. Blueprints complement rather than replace papers---the paper remains the narrative interface, the blueprint becomes the verification interface---and are designed to trade an upfront generation cost for cheaper, more local, more

41e9fbad3c82394d56fbb091.title_original: Examining the Impact of Data and Training Methods on Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment
41e9fbad3c82394d56fbb091.excerpt: arXiv:2605.12798v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Post-training a language model can induce surprising behavioral changes far beyond the intended training target. We study two particularly striking examples: emergent misalignment (EM), where fine-tuning on a narrow dataset leads to misaligned behavior in unrelated contexts, and subliminal learning (SL), where a student model inherits a teacher's misalignment through seemingly benign training data. We examine how the training data, evaluation data, and training method shape where and how strongly misalignment transfers between data and models. We characterize the data by the domain of a prompt (its topical context) and its task (the function the model performs), and we build natural-language and synthetic datasets organized as domain-task grids. We find that EM transfers more strongly to prompts that share the task of the fine-tuning data than to prompts that share its domain. In the synthetic setting, tasks that the model has learned well spread misalignment more broadly. For SL, we go beyond SFT (supervised fine-tuning) to off-policy distillation on the teacher's full next-token distribution and, to our knowledge for the first time, on-policy distillation, where the teacher only scores tokens sampled by the student. Misalignment transfers even under on-policy distillation, more strongly than under SFT and at a level comparable to off-policy distillation. Unlike SFT, where the teacher both generates the data and super

45483f93e463a5bf8713f1fc.title_original: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
45483f93e463a5bf8713f1fc.excerpt: arXiv:2605.14786v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As LLM-based agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, a natural question arises: can websites passively identify which underlying model powers an agent? Doing so would represent a significant security risk, enabling targeted attacks tailored to known model vulnerabilities. Across 14 frontier LLMs and four web environments spanning information retrieval and shopping tasks, we show that an agent's actions and interaction timings, captured via a passive JavaScript tracker, are sufficient to identify the underlying model with up to 96\% F1 within a fixed harness. Although fingerprints are harness-specific, with cross-harness transfer falling to near chance, pooling traces across harnesses recovers model identification at 0.74 to 0.81 Macro-F1. We further show that strong classifiers can be trained from roughly one third of the available traces, and that identification improves steadily as more events are observed. Injecting randomised timing delays between actions substantially degrades classifier performance, but does not provide robust protection: a classifier retrained on delayed traces largely recovers performance. We release our code and a labelled corpus of agent traces at https://github.com/KabakaWilliam/known_actions.

35db16c14fba55ca6437366b.title_original: AI-Mediated Communication Can Steer Collective Opinion
35db16c14fba55ca6437366b.excerpt: arXiv:2605.16245v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into the online platforms where humans exchange opinions; large language models (LLMs) have been polishing users' posts on LinkedIn and providing context for content shared on X. While prior work has shown that AI can express biased opinions and shape individuals' opinions during human-AI interactions, less attention has been paid to its influence on collective opinion formation when mediating human-to-human communication. We address this gap via a combination of empirical and theoretical analyses. We show empirically that LLMs from multiple popular families introduce directional biases when instructed to edit human-written texts on contested topics, for example, nudging texts in favor of gun control and against atheism. Building on this observation, we introduce a mathematical model of opinion dynamics in which an AI system sits between users on a social network, transforming the opinions they express and perceive. By analytically characterizing the equilibrium of this model and performing simulations on real social network data, we show that biases introduced by AI in human-to-human communication can be amplified through the network and shift collective opinion in their direction. In light of these findings, we investigate whether such biases are controllable by online platforms. We audit the "Explain this post" feature on X and find evidence of pro-l

0b318e1c1d9bda052ec6873f.title_original: Automated Root-Cause Subclassification and No-Code Fix Generation for Invalid Bug Reports
0b318e1c1d9bda052ec6873f.excerpt: arXiv:2605.17561v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Issues faced when using software are reported in the form of bug reports. However, many bug reports are invalid, meaning they do not require code changes, and are resolved with a no-code fix. Manually determining the root cause of the invalid bug reports and providing actionable resolutions by the customer support causes a serious waste of resources. Our goal is to introduce a standardized taxonomy for root-cause oriented invalid bug report subclassification, and perform experiments to test the accuracy of various approaches on invalid subclassification and no-code fix generation. We study how different configurations perform on a gold-standard benchmark we have created. Using a manually curated benchmark for higher quality analysis, we experimented with vanilla LLMs, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and agentic web search to identify invalid subclasses and generate no-code fixes. We evaluated the results against manually labeled ground truth data that includes the invalid subclass and no-code fixes from the original bug reports. We measured subclass detection performance with weighted F1-Score, and assessed no-code fix suggestions using BERTScore and Judge LLM success rates. For subclassification, retrieval augmented generation achieves the highest overall performance with 0.66 weighted F1, slightly outperforming vanilla LLMs at 0.65 and agentic web search at 0.64. At the subclass level, performance peaks at 0.85 F1 fo

85037fbc6643f91c09d116e8.excerpt: arXiv:2605.18760v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) faces significant challenges in complex relational retrieval tasks, particularly in densely connected knowledge graphs where the number of possible paths grows rapidly with reasoning depth. Existing GraphRAG retrieval algorithms either rely on rigid, predefined heuristics to identify relevant graph context or employ costly LLM-based reasoning to guide graph traversal. To address these limitations, we propose DotRAG, a lightweight, training-free GraphRAG retrieval algorithm that uses large language model (LLM) reasoning to narrow the search space and recover task-relevant relational paths. During indexing, DotRAG constructs an entity-relation knowledge graph, generates a graph-wide overview summarizing its contents, and leverages graph reachability indexing to avoid expensive online graph traversals. At query time, the LLM uses this overview to identify promising graph regions and hypothesizes relationship sequences connecting graph information to the query. The LLM then performs targeted relational searches, using graph constraints to restrict the candidate pool progressively. On MetaQA 2-hop queries, DotRAG achieves 97.78% retrieval recall and 51.27% F1, compared to the best baseline scores of 34.74% and 6.33%, respectively. On STaRK-MAG, DotRAG achieves 85.07% recall on 2-hop queries while demonstrating greater computational efficiency than reasoning-based GraphRAG base

cb6850bafc3bcada03c0c40a.title_original: Variance Reduction for Gradients from Diffusion Teachers
cb6850bafc3bcada03c0c40a.excerpt: arXiv:2605.21489v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pretrained diffusion models serve as frozen teachers for pipelines such as text-to-3D, single-step distillation, and data attribution. The teacher gradients these pipelines consume are expectations over noise levels and Gaussian noise, estimated by Monte Carlo (MC). Each MC draw requires expensive upstream work (rendering, simulation, encoding), so estimator variance dominates compute cost. We introduce CARV, a compute-aware variance-accounting framework that casts these gradients as a classical two-stage sampling problem with asymmetric per-level costs. This motivates a hierarchical MC estimator that amortizes each expensive upstream computation by reusing it across cheap diffusion draws, with within-unit variance further reduced by timestep importance sampling (IS) and stratified inverse-CDF sampling. CARV delivers 2 to 3x effective compute multipliers on text-to-3D and data attribution without changing the objective. In text-to-3D, reuse provides most of the gain and IS with stratification adds about 25%. In single-step distillation, the same techniques cut gradient variance by an order of magnitude but do not improve downstream FID, marking the regime where MC variance is no longer the bottleneck.

726bf8a30aa72a58386ceb74.title_original: AnyMo: Geometry-Aware Setup-Agnostic Modeling of Human Motion in the Wild
726bf8a30aa72a58386ceb74.excerpt: arXiv:2605.22715v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As wearable and mobile devices become increasingly embedded in daily life, they offer a practical way to continuously sense human motion in the wild. But inertial signals are highly dependent on the sensing setup, including body location, mounting position, sensor orientation, device hardware, and sampling protocol. This setup dependence makes it difficult to learn motion representations that transfer across devices and datasets, and limits the broader use of wearable IMUs beyond closed-set recognition. We introduce AnyMo, a geometry-aware framework for setup-agnostic human motion modeling. AnyMo uses physics-grounded IMU simulation over dense body-surface placements to generate diverse and plausible synthetic signals, pre-trains a graph encoder from paired synthetic placement views and masked partial observations, tokenizes multi-position IMU into full-body motion tokens, and aligns these tokens with an LLM for motion-language understanding. We evaluate AnyMo on three complementary tasks: zero-shot activity recognition across 14 unseen downstream datasets, cross-modal retrieval, and wearable IMU motion captioning, where it improves average Accuracy/F1/R@2 by 11.7\%/11.6\%/22.6\% on HAR, increases zero-shot IMU-to-text and text-to-IMU retrieval MRR by 15.9\% and 28.6\%, respectively, and improves zero-shot captioning BERT-F1 by 7.5\%. These results support AnyMo as a generalist model for wearable motion understanding i

1414ae35b3577a0c1326022a.title_original: Diff-Instruct with Diffused Reward: Towards Principled One-step Generator RL
1414ae35b3577a0c1326022a.excerpt: arXiv:2605.24001v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in one-step text-to-image generation have enabled real-time synthesis with remarkable efficiency and quality. Previous reinforcement learning methods for one-step generators combine image-space reward optimization with diffusion noisy-space distribution matching. This paradigm brings challenges due to a mismatch between terminal reward optimization and the underlying generative dynamics. As a result, optimization tends to exploit stochastic degrees of freedom, often improving reward at the expense of image fidelity. To address this issue, we propose Diff-Instruct with Diffused Reward (DIDR), a data-free trajectory-level alignment framework derived from Integral KL minimization. DIDR propagates the RLHF-optimal reward-tilted clean-image distribution across all noise levels along the diffusion trajectory. We show that this objective admits the same minimizer as clean-image RLHF, while naturally inducing the Diffused Reward Score (DRS), which acts as a reward-driven correction to the reference score function. To make this practical, we further introduce the Diffused Reward Proxy (DRP), an efficient estimator of DRS based on differentiable short-step denoising. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DIDR consistently Pareto-dominates existing one-step SDXL baselines. Moreover, when transferred to a 6B DiT backbone (Z-Image), DIDR surpasses its 50-step teacher in preference alignment while requiring only a s

7e264feff7afd4c595c69779.title_original: StakeBench: Evaluating Language Understanding Grounded in Market Commitment
7e264feff7afd4c595c69779.excerpt: arXiv:2605.26074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Existing financial NLP benchmarks often rely on labels supplied by outside observers, measuring how language is perceived rather than what speakers have committed to in the market. We introduce StakeBench, an evaluation framework for language understanding grounded in market commitment. StakeBench links 560,876 comments from 2,261 resolved markets to verified position, action, and market-odds records across Polymarket and Manifold. Supervision is derived from observable market behavior. Position sides, post-comment trading actions, and market-odds trajectories replace human annotation. Four diagnostic tasks test whether models detect market commitment, identify the revealed side, anticipate future action, and perform collective odds projection. Three commitment-aware metrics measure alignment with revealed preferences rather than perceived sentiment. Validity audits and explicit interpretation boundaries help distinguish observable commitment signals from latent belief and causal market-odds impact. Across 15 LLMs and 18 topics and platform settings, models partially recover position-side signals, with Directed Accuracy from 0.506 to 0.599, but show structural failures on later tasks. Ten of the fifteen models collapse to one or two action labels in future action anticipation, and no model consistently improves on the naive odds-direction baseline in collective odds projection. Model scale is not correlated with perfor

17d26d9da7fc2a3084ac9654.title_original: Unified Panoramic Geometry Estimation via Multi-View Foundation Models
17d26d9da7fc2a3084ac9654.excerpt: arXiv:2605.26368v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometry estimation from perspective images has greatly advanced, maturing to the point where off-the-shelf foundation models are able to reconstruct 3D scene structure not only from multi-view imagery, but even from a single view. A natural extension is 3D reconstruction from panoramas, with the exciting prospect of recovering a full 360-degree scene from a single panoramic image. In this work, we introduce PaGeR (Panoramic Geometry Reconstruction), a framework to lift powerful 3D foundation models designed for perspective imagery to the panorama domain. Our strategy is to start from a pre-trained transformer for 3D reconstruction and turn it into a unified high-performance model that predicts scale-invariant depth, metric depth, surface normals, and sky masks from both perspective and omnidirectional images, in a single forward pass. By keeping architectural changes to a minimum and mixing perspective and panoramic images during training, PaGeR retains the rich 3D prior of the underlying foundation model while learning to also estimate geometrically consistent 360-degree scenes from single panoramas. We extensively test our method in both indoor and outdoor environments and find that it delivers state-of-the-art performance and excellent zero-shot performance across a wide range of scenes. Code, data and models are available $\href{https://github.com/prs-eth/PaGeR}{\text{here}}$.

aed177babe48ff6e7b5d053b.title_original: Unified Synthesis of Compositional Speech and Sound from Free-Form Text Prompts
aed177babe48ff6e7b5d053b.excerpt: arXiv:2605.28063v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generating unified audio that naturally integrates speech and sounds from free-form text prompts remains challenging. For example, the prompt ``A fast drum roll ends with a cymbal crash, after which a man shouts: `Come on!'.'' describes several events that should appear in order and form a coherent recording rather than independent tracks that lack coherent temporal and semantic interactions. Current methods broadly follow two paradigms: pipeline methods couple separate text-to-sound and text-to-speech models, while unified models rely on a single generator that still requires structured, multi-field prompt inputs. Both paradigms require upstream prompt decomposition or rewriting, limiting free-form flexibility and risking cascading errors. To enable direct generation from free-form prompts within a single model, we introduce PlanAudio, an end-to-end framework that maps unconstrained free-form text to unified audio without intermediate prompt preprocessing. To address the challenges of direct free-form generation, PlanAudio integrates latent planning into a single autoregressive framework, predicting continuous audio layout before acoustic token synthesis. We construct a large-scale training corpus and introduce Free-Form Unified Audio Generation Benchmark (FUAG) for evaluation, both spanning speech, sound, and joint speech-and-sound generation. Experiments show that a single PlanAudio outperforms existing pipeline and

bd619cbf3f2c7a4fa92359ee.title_original: Pruning and Distilling Mixture-of-Experts into Dense Language Models
bd619cbf3f2c7a4fa92359ee.excerpt: arXiv:2605.28207v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is now the dominant architecture for frontier language models, yet it requires all expert parameters to be loaded in memory, making it less preferable for memory-constrained deployment. Existing compression methods reduce the number of experts but the output remains an MoE model with the same fundamental limitation. We present the first systematic framework for converting a trained MoE into a standard fully dense architecture: experts are scored, selected, and grouped, then concatenated into a dense FFN and refined by knowledge distillation from the MoE teacher. We evaluate 7 scoring, 5 grouping, and 2 magnitude scaling methods across a range of selected expert counts on Qwen3-30B-A3B, yielding 350 configurations. We find that the choice of scoring method is the most impactful, with our novel diversity-aware scoring consistently outperforming prior methods on Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and GPT-OSS-20B. Under a controlled comparison at matched parameter count, MoE-to-dense outperforms dense-to-dense pruning by +6.3 pp in average downstream accuracy after ~4B-token distillation at 1.6x faster training wall-clock speed.

c199a58f5f96765afe185582.title_original: With Tools or Because of Tools? Tracing Capability Gains in Multimodal Agents
c199a58f5f96765afe185582.excerpt: arXiv:2606.02357v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tool-augmented multimodal agents show strong benchmark gains, often taken as evidence that agents have learned to use tools. We argue that this interpretation can be premature: a tool-call trace alone does not show whether the tool supplied answer-critical information. We study two representative ``thinking with images'' agents, Thyme and DeepEyesV2, across real-world understanding, OCR, chart understanding, and mathematical reasoning. Each agent is compared with its Tool-Free counterpart and with a Pure-Text Reasoner trained from the same source pool without tool-calling trajectories. Tool access yields little consistent aggregate improvement, does not reliably reduce generated-token cost, and leaves only a small tool-only solved set: 93% of DeepEyesV2's tool-solved problems and 96% of Thyme's are also solved by at least one non-tool setting. Mechanism ablations further show that the full tool-use loop does not consistently outperform either the tool-call format or the returned execution result alone. In the settings we study, the analyzed agents appear to learn tool-calling patterns more reliably than tool-contributed capabilities, suggesting that evaluation should distinguish tool availability from whether tools actually expand what agents can solve.

4e7075d00c3afc61f2fe7c9f.title_original: From Architecture to Output: Testing the Structural Origins of Hallucination and the Amplifying Role of Data
4e7075d00c3afc61f2fe7c9f.excerpt: arXiv:2606.07537v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Surveys of hallucination classify errors by how an output relates to its source, and often explain them by the model's structure: attention retrieves by association, the maximum-likelihood objective has no term for truth, and left-to-right decoding commits to early tokens. Data, on this account, makes these failures worse rather than causing them. The account is usually argued rather than tested. We test it with interventions that need only sampling access. Study 1 holds pretraining data, tokenizer and scale fixed and swaps attention for a state-space mixer, using five Pythia/Mamba pairs from 130M to 2.8B parameters and four further attention models, on 111 facts presented with a planted false or a planted true statement. Swapping the mixer leaves free-recall failure unchanged (both 2.8B models answer 3 of 200 SimpleQA questions), but it changes what happens to a defect in the input. From 410M upwards, every attention model repeats the planted falsehood more often than its matched state-space model (2.8B: 650 vs. 566 of 666 items, p = 2.5e-20), also on facts both models know, while the state-space models can still read planted facts they did not know. Study 2 replaces the first wrong fact in 111 erroneous answers from three instruction-tuned models. The correct fact cuts the share of answers with a downstream error from 92.5% to 48.1%, but a different wrong fact works as well (p = 0.38), and the models give the right a

1236d84ede5ada2fc0b6f0df.title_original: Self-Modeling Interventions can Modulate Emergent Misalignment
1236d84ede5ada2fc0b6f0df.excerpt: arXiv:2606.23700v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Emergent misalignment (EM) has been linked to the activation of misaligned persona vectors and evil character traits, suggesting that EM operates through disruption of the model's aligned character rather than direct learning of harmful content. Motivated by this connection, we study self-modeling interventions: specifically self-recognition and self-reports as character-targeted interventions that are distinct from existing in-training defenses. We conduct two-stage finetuning experiments across three models (GPT-4.1, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct) and multiple EM datasets to compare self-recognition finetuning against benign finetuning baselines (correct domain-specific data, general knowledge, and word counting), finding it an effective defense in both reversal and prevention settings. For prevention, only self-recognition finetuning consistently reduces misalignment without exacerbating any individual metric, suggesting that character fortification specifically drives prevention. We also conduct in-training experiments across these models to compare the effectiveness of self-reports with benign interleaving and inoculation prompting. We provide further evidence for EM's relation to the LLM's default character by showing that EM finetuning leads to fragmentation of LLM's identity self-reports, reduces self-recognition performance to about chance, artificially corrupting self-recognition exacerbates mis

999cdd6861b39cfa6c1307b5.title_original: Learning Dexterous Manipulation Using Contact Wrench Guidance From Human Demonstration
999cdd6861b39cfa6c1307b5.excerpt: arXiv:2607.00033v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dexterous robot manipulation can benefit from the abundance of human demonstrations, but transferring such demonstrations to robot policies remains challenging. We present Contact Wrench Guidance from Human Demonstration in Robotic Dexterous Manipulation (CHORD), a framework for long-horizon manipulation of rigid and articulated objects with reinforcement learning. The key idea is object-centric contact wrench space guidance: we represent human and robot motions by the forces and torques they can induce on the object, enabling similarity to be measured by the induced instantaneous motions. This guidance makes reinforcement learning more scalable for contact-rich dexterous manipulation. We further introduce a large-scale simulation benchmark with 4,739 bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks, constructed from motion-capture datasets and reconstructed in-house videos. Evaluated on 1,831 benchmark tasks, CHORD achieves an average success rate of 82.12%, demonstrating strong scalability. CHORD also generalizes to whole-body manipulation from hand-only and third-person demonstrations, achieving a 90.77% success rate, and the learned policies transfer to the real world in both open-loop and closed-loop settings.

c3558a583eb1c2e77de18355.title_original: Adaptive Reparametrized Time for Score-Based Diffusion Sampling
c3558a583eb1c2e77de18355.excerpt: arXiv:2607.02137v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study timestep allocation for score-based diffusion sampling, where a learned reverse-time dynamics is discretized on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted schedules are standard choices, but they rely on fixed prescriptions and can therefore be suboptimal. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), a continuous-time control formulation that learns a time change by treating the speed of the sampling clock as the control, so that a uniform grid on the learned clock induces adaptive timesteps in the original diffusion time. Based on a leading-order Euler error surrogate, ART provides a principled objective for allocating timesteps along the sampling trajectory. To solve this deterministic control problem, we introduce ART-RL, an auxiliary randomized formulation with Gaussian policies that turns schedule learning into a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem. We prove that the randomized ART-RL formulation is equivalent to ART at the optimizer level, in the sense that its optimal Gaussian policy recovers the optimal ART time-warping rate through its mean. We further establish policy evaluation and policy improvement characterizations and derive trajectory-based moment identities that yield implementable actor--critic updates for learning the schedule. Across experiments ranging from controlled low-dimensional settings to image generation, ART-RL can be plugged into existing di

94591c58c5b39aa33c9d2b53.title_original: Listen to the Features: Voice Anonymization Driven by Content Embedding Matching over Signal Reconstruction
94591c58c5b39aa33c9d2b53.excerpt: arXiv:2607.09767v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The paper presents a voice anonymization model focusing on preserving content rather than producing realistic speech. It relies on content embeddings extracted from a frozen pretrained wav2vec2 encoder. These embeddings are decoded into an anonymized signal using vector quantization and a HiFi-GAN vocoder, both trained on LibriTTS without any waveform reconstruction loss or speaker embedding mapping. The training objective enforces that embeddings of the anonymized signal match those of the original one. While training, an auxiliary speaker classification branch with a gradient reversal layer is used to discard speakerspecific information. Results show that this straightforward embedding-based approach achieves very low WER (2.53) with an anonymization performance (EER 13.39) ranking within first level for VPC. Notably, emotions are partially preserved (UAR 43.91), even without a supporting training objective, while the anonymized voice is audible without reconstruction loss.

f1172db370ce306b8dc9a52e.title_original: RamanPFN: A physics-guided spectral foundation framework for in-context learning across diverse Raman applications
f1172db370ce306b8dc9a52e.excerpt: arXiv:2608.02157v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Raman spectroscopy enables label-free molecular characterization across materials science, analytical chemistry, biomedicine, and industrial process monitoring. However, machine learning for high-dimensional spectroscopy remains constrained by limited labeled data and a mismatch between the physical organization of spectra and feature-agnostic models. Tabular foundation models such as TabPFN predict in context without parameter updates, but on wide spectra feature subsampling preserves channel coverage while losing joint visibility: in the five widest tasks, every channel was covered, yet only 4.4% of random channel pairs co-occurred in any forward pass. We present RamanPFN, a general-purpose spectral foundation framework for unified in-context inference through physics-guided spectral learning, which encodes the additive mixing of constituent spectra and the locality of vibrational bands. Global Compositional Unmixing decomposes distributed, multi-band mixture signatures into shared non-negative bases to couple covarying peaks across the full spectrum, while Local Vibrational Subspace Encoding extracts orthogonal modes within contiguous spectral neighborhoods to preserve peak morphology, intensity fluctuations, and peak shifts. Posterior marginalization over admissible unmixings unifies both scales into in-context prediction without updating the model. Across 74 public Raman datasets exceeding 330,000 spectra, RamanPF

2a6a08a9ab5d956e7f99bce2.title_original: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
2a6a08a9ab5d956e7f99bce2.excerpt: arXiv:2608.09928v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) exhibit strong visual understanding, yet the internal features that cause these behaviors remain difficult to identify, audit, or control. While applicable to post-hoc inspection, hidden states that are decomposed into interpretable feature directions using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) neither readily isolate which features are changed by multimodal training, nor are they directly useful for targeted control. We introduce MMDiff, a multimodal model-diffing framework that trains multimodal SAEs and turns them into feature-level interfaces for discovering and controlling multimodal behavior. MMDiff supports three uses: (i) feature isolation, by diffing a base-LM SAE against its multimodal-adapted counterpart to identify features altered by multimodal training; (ii) task-specific feature detection, via per-token contrastive firing analysis that isolates causal features; and (iii) feature-level control, by causally removing or steering the discovered feature directions. We train multimodal SAEs for three MLLM families, LLaVA-MORE, PaliGemma 2, and InternVL3.5, and evaluate on visual-spatial understanding, multimodal safety, and OCR. MMDiff discovers sparse, causally specific features whose removal selectively degrades target behaviors by an average of 12% on spatial tasks and 17% on OCR, and reduces attack success rate by 24% on multimodal safety attacks, with no impact on VQA perform

0ef7c36659b7628a465d5cfb.title_original: SplitLite: Low-Rank Residual Compression for Split Learning
0ef7c36659b7628a465d5cfb.excerpt: arXiv:2608.23018v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Federated fine-tuning of on-device large language models (LLMs) faces a significant computing burden. To overcome this limitation, split learning (SL) has emerged as a promising solution, which offloads the primary training workload to a powerful server. However, SL requires exchanging high-dimensional activations and gradients between clients and the server, resulting in prohibitive communication costs. To overcome this challenge, we propose SplitLite, a communication-efficient split federated LoRA fine-tuning method that exploits the low effective rank structure of consecutive-epoch activation and gradient residuals. Our key finding is that, under low-rank LoRA updates with the pretrained backbone frozen, the activation and gradient residuals of the same data sample between adjacent epochs exhibit low effective ranks, with most of their energy concentrated in a small number of singular directions. By exploiting this property, SplitLite transmits only quantized truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) residual factors, thereby significantly reducing both activation uplink and gradient downlink traffic. Extensive experiments on the GLUE benchmark across a series of advanced on-device LLMs demonstrate that our method reduces activation uplink communication costs by up to 93.5\% and total communication costs by up to 88.6\%, without sacrificing model performance.

b237303ab16ef0f1c5531a3f.title_original: Reinforcement Learning over Patient Trajectories for Clinical Reasoning in EHR Foundation Models
b237303ab16ef0f1c5531a3f.excerpt: arXiv:2609.12277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Electronic health record (EHR) foundation models trained on longitudinal patient trajectories have demonstrated strong performance across diverse clinical prediction tasks. However, their clinical reasoning capabilities remain constrained by next-token prediction on limited and incomplete EHR data. To address this, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning framework that treats EHR foundation models as generative policies over patient trajectories. We formulate common clinical prediction problems (e.g., hospital readmission) as event-conditioned, time-windowed reasoning tasks. We then design time-aware, rollout-sensitive rewards to account for finite rollout lengths and temporally inconclusive outcomes. We find that RL fine-tuning consistently improves over pre-trained backbones and strong baselines. Notably, it enables smaller models to match larger pre-trained models in data-limited regimes and induces positive transfer across tasks. Further analysis shows that RL fine-tuned models generate trajectories with stronger structural and semantic alignment to ground truth and greater downstream utility.

7b6e09ed7736c0d099dc0541.title_original: GraphToolbox: A Configurable Framework for Controlled Benchmarking of Graph Neural Network Forecasting
7b6e09ed7736c0d099dc0541.excerpt: arXiv:2609.24609v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Electricity forecasting often involves spatially related signals observed over regions, substations, and feeders, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) represent these relations through a graph. Building a complete GNN forecasting experiment is nonetheless laborious, because graph construction, model selection, training, aggregation, and interpretation often require separate tools. We present GraphToolbox, an open-source Python framework that unifies these stages in one configuration-driven pipeline built on PyTorch Geometric. It offers data-driven graph construction, a single interface for most graph convolution operators of PyTorch Geometric and for recurrent graph cells, online expert aggregation, forecasting interpretability, and significance testing on forecasts. We use GraphToolbox to run a controlled benchmark: we compare architectural and modeling choices for French electricity load and net-load forecasting at regional and national levels under a common experimental protocol. On load, most evaluated graph convolutions outperform additive, recurrent, and foundation-model baselines. Pooled XGBoost, trained on the same inputs, has a lower RMSE than the best graph models, although the difference is not significant. Online expert aggregation and daily model updates improve accuracy further. On net-load, graph models outperform additive, recurrent, and XGBoost baselines, with further gains from forecasting the physical co

7a5246bb47d515d3634e1f04.title_original: Learning Perturbation Robust Policies for LLM Agents with Stable Optimization
7a5246bb47d515d3634e1f04.excerpt: arXiv:2609.34064v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an effective post-training paradigm for long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents. However, we find that the resulting policies can be sensitive to various policy perturbations, such as hidden-state noise, pruning, and quantization. In this work, we study how to improve perturbation robustness during policy optimization. We first introduce the notion of a perturbation robust policy and analyze conditions under which perturbed policy updates preserve stable monotonic improvement. Based on this analysis, we introduce Stable Perturbation-Robust Policy Optimization (SPrPO), which applies adaptive and sensitivity-aware perturbations during RL training. We evaluate SPrPO on ALFWorld and WebShop and conduct systematic experiments across multiple perturbation types and scales, showing improved perturbation robustness while maintaining stable policy optimization.

bf32f6fb66888e074851e8b8.title_original: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
bf32f6fb66888e074851e8b8.excerpt: arXiv:2609.38166v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent LLMs increasingly adopt hybrid designs that replace standard attention with linear attention, such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA). Although they compress the context into a fixed-size recurrent state and substantially reduce the cost of long-context processing, repeatedly reading and updating that state remains a major inference bottleneck. Quantization offers a natural way to reduce this cost, but can significantly degrade model quality, due to the accumulation of rounding errors and the presence of outlier rows and columns in the state. To address these challenges, we propose LeapQuant, a training-free method that achieves near-lossless performance under 8-bit recurrent-state quantization. First, to mitigate error accumulation, we propose per-window quantization, which leaps over a window of tokens and quantizes the state only once at its end. Within a window, outputs are computed from the fixed low-bit state together with high-precision buffered updates. Second, to reduce the error introduced by each quantization, LeapQuant retains the state's largest outliers as a few high-precision Compensator Tokens, which share the update path of real tokens. We then smooth the remaining residual before quantization to further reduce the error. Comprehensive experiments across the Qwen, Kimi, and GLM model families show that LeapQuant substantially reduces memory and compute costs during inference.

d3802ece0222ebcae90679c0.title_original: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in LLMs with Whiteout
d3802ece0222ebcae90679c0.excerpt: arXiv:2610.02418v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) are trained on massive, largely unfiltered datasets, including content scraped from nearly every accessible website and user inputs. As a result, LLMs often memorize and reproduce personally sensitive information (PSI) such as birth dates, phone numbers, and home addresses. This leads to significant privacy risks, particularly for high-profile individuals such as executives, politicians, and judges. Existing mitigations largely rely on machine unlearning. However, these methods often remove more information than needed, degrade model utility and safety, and are highly vulnerable to attacks. This paper presents Whiteout, a practical tool that, upon requests by individuals, prevents LLMs from regurgitating their genuine PSIs, by overwriting them using precise and carefully designed obfuscation samples. We evaluate Whiteout on modern LLMs of varying sizes and makers, including a widely-used OpenAI model. Results show that Whiteout effectively prevents disclosure of the targeted PSIs, has negligible impact on model utility and safety, and outperforms existing alternatives. We also test Whiteout against a wide range of countermeasures, from black-box attacks like jailbreaking to white-box adaptive attacks like relearning and quantization. Finally, we conclude with a discussion on the security and ethical implications of Whiteout.

11587454aa805780213a3d99.title_original: CACHEFORGE: LLM-Guided End-to-End Generative Cache Replacement Policy for Performance and Hardware Efficiency
11587454aa805780213a3d99.excerpt: arXiv:2610.07668v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modern cache replacement designs saturate because they operate within fixed representational structures, hand-crafted and heuristic based feature-engineered predictors, or offline imitation models that cannot generate new decision logic on their own. At the same time, replacement is shaped by the causal interaction of prefetching, thrashing, spatial locality, and access-type behavior, producing an enormous design space that is difficult to traverse manually. Prior approaches typically rely on heuristics, parameter tuning, or imitation of an offline optimal policy, capturing correlations rather than synthesizing new mechanisms. As a result, their performance gains often plateau and they overfit under dynamic workload conditions. CACHEFORGE is the first framework to evolve cache-replacement policies end-to-end by embedding a large language model inside a governed hardware-aware loop. In each iteration, the LLM proposes new C++ replacement logic, the policy is evaluated under a trace-based CRC-2 ChampSim simulator, and the framework enforces feasibility through reward shaping, structural checks, dynamic mutation, temperature scheduling, and cross-policy crossover. This closed-loop generation-evolution loop specifically designed for cache replacement policy enables the discovery of compact policies that satisfy hardware constraints while exploring algorithmic transformations beyond fixed predictor structures. Across SPEC C

6a257e3f018a1dcfe2759bea.title_original: Where Polanyi Meets Galois: Tacit Knowing as an Algebro-Deterministic Operation, Toward Re-rooting AI-Generated Science
6a257e3f018a1dcfe2759bea.excerpt: arXiv:2610.16102v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tacit knowing, we argue, is an operating regime of one memory substrate, not a separate kind of content. In VaCoAl, an algebro-deterministic hyperdimensional memory over $\mathrm{GF}(2)$ realized as CASRAM and PyVaCoAl, one DAG of bound records is read in two ways. With every collision repaired (Rescue), the trace is exactly auditable but no path outranks another; with collisions tolerated (Don't Care), a path-integrated confidence $\mathrm{CR}_2$ ranks direct over circuitous routes without being stated. This audit-valuation complementarity formalizes Polanyi's claim that tacit and explicit knowledge are not sharply divided. (1) Polanyi's from-to structure reads as non-commutative binding. (2) Full explication destroys the valuation (Lemma 1), as with Polanyi's pianist; tacitness is thus contingent or regime-bound, placing Polanyi, Nonaka, Tsoukas and Collins on one substrate. (3) The same lemma answers a second dualism: the popular dual-process moral ("train slow, deliberate System 2 to tame fast, intuitive System 1") mirrors the two-store reading of tacit and explicit knowledge Polanyi rejected. Mercier and Sperber's reply, that reasoning is intuitive inference about reasons, matches Polanyi's; in the substrate, complete supervision is full rescue, which erases the valuation it should discipline. (4) Collins's three tacit knowledges map to bound structure, substrate valuation and value binding. (5) Our mentor-student

220dbd46ff5cd31df04237ba.title_original: Prune-and-Merge: Training-Free Scaling of Vision Transformers
220dbd46ff5cd31df04237ba.excerpt: arXiv:2610.18039v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision Transformers achieve strong performance but incur high computational costs from quadratic token interactions. Training-free token reduction methods improve efficiency, but their robustness remains underexplored. We propose Prune-and Merge ViT, a training-free framework for off-the-shelf models. It combines class attention-based pruning with similarity-based merging to reduce redundancy while preserving semantic information. To evaluate robustness we introduce two metrics. Relative Accuracy Drop (RAD) measures relative accuracy degradation under transformations, and Prediction Flip Rate (PFR) quantifies prediction consistency. On pretrained ViT and DeiT, Prune-and-Merge reduces computation competitively while maintaining robustness and better accuracy than existing token reduction methods. Our analysis suggests that hybrid token reduction does not introduce hallucination-like behavior and preserves prediction stability for common image transformations.

141bbe3c6dfbdedd1b866cc2.title_original: Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss
141bbe3c6dfbdedd1b866cc2.excerpt: arXiv:2610.36202v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Persona Selection Model (PSM) posits that post-training selects a persona the model learned during pre-training. Work on subliminal learning has shown that models can impart covert signals (like "love of owls") into semantically unrelated outputs like strings of numbers, and that students trained on these outputs inherit those traits. In this work I show that by evaluating the likelihood of such outputs under the base pre-trained model with an appropriate header, a method I call persona-header likelihood evaluation (PHLE), one can decode these subliminal signals and classify between them. For example, PHLE distinguishes number sequences generated by a post-trained model prompted with "You love owls" from those prompted with "You love trains", and distinguishes answers from a model with a secret desire to harm the user, filtered to remove any noticeable misalignment, from those of a model with no system prompt. In both cases prompted classifiers, including the generating model itself, perform far worse. The signal partially persists across model families, with the Qwen base model reading signals generated by Olmo and vice versa. This is evidence for a non-trivial prediction of the PSM, and the method may be practically useful for auditing the hidden objectives of models.

42316704ecd64b2a6c346d3a.title_original: Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer for Joint Multipath Parameter Estimation: Applications to mmWave Positioning and Radio SLAM
42316704ecd64b2a6c346d3a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.01491v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Future 6G wireless networks are expected to evolve toward AI-native systems that support intelligent, environment-aware services, including positioning and mapping. Current research has already integrated AI into several aspects of communication, particularly wireless channel estimation. However, most learning-based channel estimators focus on communication-oriented objectives rather than explicitly estimating multipath parameters such as delay, angle of arrival (AoA), and angle of departure (AoD). These parameters provide essential geometric information for downstream tasks including positioning and radio simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). In this work, we propose a Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer (SCFT) for joint multipath component (MPC) estimation from noisy complex channel estimates and physical beam-pair descriptors. SCFT combines local spectral convolution, permutation-equivariant beam-set attention, and a query-based Transformer decoder to detect and classify line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight paths and estimate their observed delays, AoAs, and AoDs. Experiments on realistic ray-tracing data show that SCFT reduces the generalized optimal sub-pattern assignment error by 13.1% compared with ResNet, the strongest competing baseline. We further demonstrate this advantage in independent snapshot positioning and radio SLAM, where SCFT reduces position RMSE by 18.5% and 65.0%, respectively, r

e2fab9a4d09a4a6c8ac70fa0.title_original: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
e2fab9a4d09a4a6c8ac70fa0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.06706v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tech-facilitated gender based violence (TFGBV) is a pervasive online harm affecting women and gender minority groups through its many direct and covert forms. Current models and annotated datasets for gendered harm detection are dominated by data from, and models trained in, Global North languages. In collaboration with civil society organizations (CSOs) from Jordan, Francophone West Africa, and Kenya, we developed a community-led approach to crowdsource culturally and linguistically relevant instances of TFGBV in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili. We annotated the crowdsourced data using active learning to develop a small but performant dataset (N=3022) called ALTO to improve TFGBV detection in the three languages. Through benchmarking and fine-tuning experiments, we show that existing harmful content detection models show poor TFGBV recall within ALTO and improve with fine-tuning. We found that models often miss covert harms across all languages, while error rates are markedly higher in Swahili. We report the experimental results and release the annotation taxonomy, dataset, and trained models.

1e8ced4054706552129c0df7.title_original: Selective Retrieval Routing for Multi-Violation Knowledge Graph Repair
1e8ced4054706552129c0df7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.07342v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Knowledge graphs often contain missing or inconsistent facts that undermine the applications built on them. Schema validation detects such violations but does not identify which of several valid repairs recovers the intended graph. External corpora can supply the evidence needed to identify the intended repair, but retrieving from them is costly and not always successful. We propose a framework for selective retrieval in iterative graph repair. An LLM repair agent explores and edits the graph, while a router controls its access to a researcher agent that retrieves external evidence. We extend a violation-injection framework to generate cases with multiple compatible violations and known reference repairs. The agent's repair outcomes on these cases provide supervision for training the deployment-specific router. On two building-automation datasets, researcher access improves repairs for some violations and degrades them for others, with effects differing across deployments. The router uses fewer repair-time tokens than always enabling access in all six evaluation suites. It achieves higher repair $F_1$ than always disabling access in five of six suites.

69f17af61249fca74bbdca0b.title_original: Towards Scalable Diagnostic-Driven Whole-Slide Image Retrieval for Pathology Archives
69f17af61249fca74bbdca0b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.07935v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The growing adoption of digital pathology has rapidly expanded collections of hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images, yet efficient navigation through these archives remains challenging, as metadata is often inconsistent or unavailable. Content-based image retrieval addresses this challenge by identifying similar cases directly from visual representations instead of manual annotations or metadata. Existing retrieval systems have demonstrated promising performance but largely rely on handcrafted indexing pipelines and predefined sampling strategies, constraining scalability and generalization. Here, we present CLEAR-WSI (Constant-Length Embedding for Automatic Retrieval of Whole-Slide Images) as a scalable, diagnostic-driven slide-retrieval framework, validated on both public and clinical data. Using a fixed-length slide embedding, CLEAR-WSI refines retrieved candidates with either a predicted diagnostic label or the ground-truth label, depending on the retrieval setting. Newly processed cases are subsequently added to the expanding memory bank, allowing the retrieval archive to grow over time. On a comprehensive benchmark consisting of two public and one private clinical datasets representing four retrieval tasks, CLEAR-WSI improves Precision@5 over the strongest evaluated baseline, with gains on CAMELYON16 (3.10), BRACS-1 (2.75), BRACS-2 (1.95), and X-HER2 (3.75). Additional ablation and latency studies further exam

42aa83520608d901003c3d26.title_original: Useful Work Can Increase Energy Use: Demand Elasticity and Proof of Useful Work
42aa83520608d901003c3d26.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A serious criticism of Bitcoin's Proof-of-Work is its enormous electricity consumption. Proof-of-Useful-Work (PoUW), introduced by Ball, Rosen, Sabin, and Vasudevan (2017), in which mining performs useful computations, was suggested as an alternative to reduce electricity expenditure, with matrix multiplication (MatMul) as a recent concrete instantiation by Komargodski and Weinstein (2026). Perhaps surprisingly, we show that switching to PoUW may increase the total electricity consumption, echoing Jevons' paradox. Intuitively, the PoUW mechanism acts as a subsidy that lowers the effective price of the useful work. Recall that demand is elastic if a discount of x percent in the price leads to an increase of more than x percent in the quantity demanded. If demand is elastic, the resulting increase in quantity demanded leads to a net increase in total electricity consumption; if inelastic, total electricity consumption decreases. Even then, the electricity consumption due to PoUW never vanishes, since the mining subsidy is spent on useful work that would not have been produced without the subsidy. This result is proved in a simple model with electricity-only costs, no PoUW overhead, and an unchanged mining subsidy. The analysis extends to less restrictive settings with adjusted thresholds.

4a091aa90c641de422441060.title_original: Splitting for Stability: a Modified Reward Scheme for Transaction-Fee-Only Regimes
4a091aa90c641de422441060.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Bitcoin's block subsidy declines over time, miner revenue will come to depend increasingly on transaction fees. In fee-dominated regimes, winner-take-all reward structures can create incentives for undercutting and fork-based mining strategies, leading to instability and reduced transaction throughput. To prevent this instability, we propose a reward-splitting mechanism in which the winning block producer receives an $\alpha$-portion of the block reward, while the rest is distributed among other miners; this incentivizes mining on previous blocks with higher rewards, while preserving the incentive to produce blocks with high rewards. We evaluate the proposed reward structure through analysis and simulation. Our analysis derives a local profitability condition for one-step Function-Fork deviations, showing how the winner-side reward, loser-side subsidy, and honest hash power jointly determine whether undercutting is profitable. Simulations show parameter regions in which honest behavior dominates fork-based deviations. In the cases where forking becomes dominant, the learned strategy is the least aggressive variant studied. The analysis and simulations suggest that suitable reward-splitting parameters can reduce the honest participation needed to suppress aggressive forking strategies relative to the winner-take-all structure studied in prior work. Finally, we show that the modified reward scheme does not appear to worsen self

fe4e05c3abd2826bbb69d6e1.title_original: Early Rug Pull Detection on Solana
fe4e05c3abd2826bbb69d6e1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web3 platforms that help users discover and trade newly launched crypto tokens, including launchpads, decentralized-exchange (DEX) interfaces, wallets, and token-analytics sites, must assess tokens before their legitimacy is clear. On Solana, where token creation is inexpensive and tokens use standard programs rather than custom per-token smart contracts, rug pulls can unfold within minutes. Effective warnings must therefore rely on limited histories. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) have improved rug-pull detection on EVM chains, it remains unclear whether transfer structure adds predictive value over non-graph models at minute-scale decision points, and how that value changes as history accumulates. We study 2,700 tokens sampled from SolRPDS, collecting one-minute market histories from Birdeye and token transfers from Solana RPC. We define a rug pull operationally by requiring a liquidity drain, price collapse, and persistent liquidity depletion over a nominal 24-hour period after token creation. All features use only information available at or before each prediction cutoff. We evaluate observation windows of 12.5, 35.5, and 93 minutes, selected in advance from the published lifespan distribution of Solana rug pulls, and represent each token as a temporal transfer graph. Within the first 12.5 minutes, rug-pull and non-rug graphs already differ in size, density, reciprocity, and receiver-side centralization. We compare GN

1f05ace792090b996bd64afa.title_original: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices
1f05ace792090b996bd64afa.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. We map an authenticated challenge-response protocol onto 5G's slot structure, replace permanent key erasure with short-lived execution leases, and specify a cross-check of the chip's reported serving cell against the carrier's own attachment records. In ns-3 and 5G-LENA simulations of an unloaded cell, our URLLC-based radio profile narrows the 99.9th percentile round-trip spread to 2.60 ms, more than ten times narrower than default 5G. A tracer rejects every round of a fiber relay from 300 km, against 2,000 km for default 5G. Against a 3,000 km attacker, a tracer stays safe at up to 1,410 km from the chip, against

785998c422f2fee62aa7e1e3.title_original: Data-Efficient Unlearning-Based Backdoor Detection in Federated Learning
785998c422f2fee62aa7e1e3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting backdoor attacks in federated learning (FL) is challenging because malicious clients can manipulate the global model while preserving main-task performance. Static model-update statistics may therefore fail to clearly distinguish malicious from benign clients. Unlearning-based detectors instead probe client models through loss ascent on clean server data, but detection performance degrades with scarce proxy data. We propose Screening via Unlearning Response Analysis (SURA), a data-efficient detector. SURA reuses the same small clean proxy across multiple train-mode loss-ascent steps, strengthening client responses without additional clean data. For federated vision models with batch normalization (BN), repeated probing also changes BN running statistics and can confound endpoint measurements. SURA addresses this by restoring the shared pre-probe BN state only at readout while preserving the parameter changes induced by probing. This separates repeated probing from response measurement and removes BN drift and the interaction between parameter and BN-state changes from the readout. Across six backdoor attacks, SURA uses only 10 clean server images, outperforms methods under the same data budget, and approaches the robustness obtained with much larger proxy sets.

34be443a5a82ec4e5177f652.title_original: TERM: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation
34be443a5a82ec4e5177f652.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across diverse applications, making both safety and utility essential for reliable deployment. Jailbreak attacks use diverse forms of adversarial prompting to bypass alignment safeguards and induce LLMs to generate harmful responses. Some representation-based defenses regulate internal activations using predefined steering directions or learned safety regions. However, adapting intervention to each input without a predefined representational target while limiting over-refusal remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose Target-free Entropy-guided Residual Modulation (TERM), an inference-time defense that uses prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to guide adaptive modulation of the model's own residual updates. Attention patterns vary across prompts and decoding steps, making raw entropy values difficult to interpret as a consistent signal for intervention. We therefore calibrate attention entropy against each prompt's own prefill baseline to establish an input-specific reference for reducing unnecessary intervention on benign requests. Adaptive scale normalization and temporal accumulation then account for differences in deviation scale and persistence to determine intervention strength. The resulting signal controls bounded scaling of the model's own residual updates, without relying on a predefined safety direction. We compare our method with seven defense
